# Maksym

> Senior Backend Engineer (Java, Spring Boot, distributed systems) with 10 years building high-traffic, regulated backend systems for banking and telco. Based in Madrid, Spain. Open to new remote opportunities in senior backend, platform or fintech engineering; authorized to work in the EU.

Currently at Openbank (Grupo Santander), building the backend for the bank's launch in Germany. Previously Simyo (via Paradigma Digital), Banco Santander and Mobile World Congress (via Experis) and Telefónica (via everis). Languages: Spanish, Russian, Ukrainian (native), English (professional).

AI assistants can query his profile directly through a public MCP server (no auth) instead of scraping this site.

## Radar

- [All issues](https://maksym.site/radar/): daily news from the LLM and AI world and backend engineering, with a short take on each (RSS and MCP available)
- [RSS](https://maksym.site/radar/feed.xml)
<!-- radar:start -->
- [Google's LiteRT Tensor API for on-device ML models](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-11-04-google-litert-tensor-api-device-ml-models/): Google's new LiteRT Tensor API lets developers build, customize, and optimize ML models for on-device execution. This could change how backend teams integrate AI into their applications.
- [LLMs can edit neural network weights: Weight Space Programming](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-11-03-llms-can-edit-neural-network-weights-weight-space-programming/): A new method lets LLMs read and edit neural network weights, potentially streamlining model training and debugging. I would verify the method's robustness before adopting it in production.
- [Agentic web: the new frontier for AI](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-11-02-agentic-web-new-frontier-ai/): The agentic web is here, transforming how AI interacts with online content. This shift brings new opportunities and challenges for backend engineering teams.
- [Docusign's contract agents and Spring's AI push](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-11-01-docusign-contract-agents-spring-ai-push/): Docusign's new contract agents and the latest Spring releases highlight the growing integration of AI in backend systems.
- [BoxLang AI 3.6 Adds Browser, Audio, and MCP Modules for JVM Agents](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-10-31-boxlang-ai-3-6-adds-browser-audio-mcp-modules-jvm-agents/): Ortus Solutions released BoxLang AI 3.6, extending its JVM-based productivity platform with browser automation, audio processing, and a stdio MCP client. The update is relevant as teams look for ways to embed agentic capabilities directly into existing Java stacks without spinning up separate runtimes.
